items.title: MACC flags governance weaknesses as root cause of leakages
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Governance weaknesses are among the most common aspects identified by the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) during preliminary investigations into leakage and misappropriation within organisations in the country. "Apart from that, we also need to investigate governance weaknesses where they exist. This issue of governance is interconnected.

items.title: Bursa Malaysia's key index opens higher before easing marginally
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia's key index opened higher on Monday before easing marginally in early trade, amid continued buying interest following Wall Street's stronger performance and easing United States-China trade tensions, an analyst said. The index opened 0.93 of-a-point higher at 1,672.55. Turnover stood at 209.81 million shares worth RM115.48 million.

items.title: Three vehicles destroyed in early morning fire at Klang apartment
items.summary: KLANG: Three vehicles, including a motorcycle, were destroyed in an early morning fire at Block B of Apartment Meru Impian in Kapar, near here, today. Selangor Fire and Rescue Department operations assistant director Ashrul Riezal Asbar said a team from the Kapar Fire and Rescue Station was dispatched to the scene after receiving an emergency call. "The operation commander reported that the fire involved three vehicles, and firefighters immediately carried out extinguishing operations using a hose reel line connected to the fire engine's water tank," he said in a statement today.

items.title: Malaysian bonds retreat as US yields, oil prices rise
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysian government bonds came under pressure last week as rising US Treasury yields and a rebound in oil prices reversed an earlier rally, according to CIMB Securities Sdn Bhd. The firm said Malaysian Government Securities (MGS) yields rose by one to four basis points week-on-week, with the 10-year yield climbing back towards four per cent after falling as low as 3.89 per cent during the week. The 30-year MGS yield rose four basis points to 4.40 per cent, while the three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (Klibor) increased three basis points to 3.51 per cent.

items.title: Malaysia, UNODC strengthen cooperation to tackle complex transnational crimes, says Saifuddin Nasution
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 28 — Malaysia aims to strengthen cooperation with the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC) through more practical and result-oriented initiatives to address the increasingly complex threat of transnational organised crime. Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the matter was discussed during his meeting with the UNODC regional representative for South-east Asia and the Pacific on the final day of his working visit to Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates (UAE), in conjunction with the 15th United Nations Congress on Crime Prevention and Criminal Justice. He said during the meeting, both sides exchanged views on the increasingly complex landscape of transnational organised crime, particularly criminal networks exploiting digital technology to expand their activities across borders and jurisdictions.

items.title: Saravanan, family members at MACC to receive asset declaration notice
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Former human resources minister Datuk Seri M Saravanan and several family members arrived at the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) headquarters here today, believed to be to receive asset declaration notices Saravanan arrived at the MACC headquarters entrance at 9.15am with his wife and two children in two black Toyota Alphard and Vellfire vehicles. On Friday, MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said the graft-busters would serve asset declaration notices on Saravanan, his wife and three children. "Saravanan, his wife and two of their children would be present at the MACC headquarters on Monday to receive the notices, while another child who is studying in London would receive the notice in November.

items.title: Ampang Jaya police probe viral TikTok assault and multi-car collision
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 28 — Police are investigating a case of vandalism and voluntarily causing hurt after a car collided with several parked vehicles and a related assault, which went viral on TikTok. After the hike, the complainant drove Nadia home to Pangsapuri Sri Intan. There, the complainant was approached by three men, one of whom knocked on the driver's-side window and told the complainant to get out.

items.title: RTD detects businesses hiring foreigners as commercial drivers
items.summary: KOTA BARU: The Road Transport Department (RTD) has detected businesses hiring foreigners to drive lorries and buses, as well as Malaysians renting motorcycles to foreigners for profit. He said foreigners were not eligible to apply for Goods Driving Licence (GDL) or Public Service Vehicle (PSV) licences to drive goods or public service vehicles. Kifli said Malaysians who rented out their vehicles to foreigners, particularly motorcycles, were also contributing to the problem.

items.title: Mohamad Hasan urges stronger Asean connectivity, eyes freer region with EU‑style movement
items.summary: NEW YORK, Sept 28 — Asean needs to continue strengthening connectivity among its member states as a step towards creating a more open and integrated region, said Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan. “Connectivity among Asean countries needs to be effective,” he said during a question-and-answer session at a gathering with the Malaysian diaspora here on Saturday. he said.

items.title: Ministry reviews university holdings, UiTM team formed to safeguard Bumiputera institution’s future
items.summary: ASTANA (Kazakhstan), Sept 28 —The Ministry of Higher Education (MOHE) began reviewing and restructuring public university holding companies last year, including UiTM Holdings Sdn Bhd, said its Minister, Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir. “We have asked for all university holdings to be reviewed. That was the first step we took, and we have already begun several rounds of reviews to reassess these holdings, including UiTM Holdings,” he said.

items.title: Evocom opens 16.67pct below IPO price on ACE Market debut
items.summary: The logistics services provider opened at 15 sen, 16.67 per cent or three sen below its IPO price of 18 sen, with 10 million shares changing hands at the opening bell. The Semenyih-based company provides manpower support for e-commerce logistics operations, alongside network support services covering last-mile delivery, transshipment and parcel shipment. The company raised RM20.5 million from its IPO, with RM7.2 million earmarked as working capital for its flexible staffing services to support existing operations.

items.title: Malaysian Embassy distributes dry food to staff and citizens hit by Bangkok floods
items.summary: BANGKOK, Sept 28 — The Malaysian Embassy in Bangkok distributed dry food supplies to 10 Malaysians and locally recruited embassy staff who were directly affected by the floods in the Thai capital. Malaysian Ambassador to Thailand Datuk Wan Zaidi Wan Abdullah said the dry food supplies, which could be stored for an extended period, were distributed to those affected on Sunday. Meanwhile, Wan Zaidi said the embassy would continue to monitor the flood situation in Bangkok and provide assistance to affected Malaysians and embassy staff.

items.title: From Mat Kilau to flying Malays: How communal anxieties fuel alternative history publishers
items.summary: Although she was dismissed by the International Islamic University Malaysia in April, her revisionist claims retain a fervent following. Boasting over 500,000 followers across Facebook and TikTok, Solehah continues to draw thousands of viewers, while her in-person Lost Malay History and Civilisation seminars remain in high demand, The Straits Times reported. Aziff Azuddin of Iman Research said: “My reading is that the multicultural landscape of Malaysia, as well as Malay socio-political and economic anxieties, is why nativists, right-wingers – and people like Solehah – have such a purchase among some sections of the Malay community.”

items.title: Heavy rain cuts off access to Pos Balar
items.summary: GUA MUSANG: Continuous heavy rain since yesterday afternoon caused a section of the main road to the Orang Asli settlement at Pos Balar here to collapse, cutting off access to all vehicles. "The route is the main access road to Pos Balar. "The paved Rural Connectivity Road project from Kuala Betis - Pos Bihai - Pos Belatim - Pos Balar - Pos Hau and back to Kuala Betis is our only hope for better access.

items.title: #NSTviral: Malaysians flex muscle and lift badly parked car to clear gridlock
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A group of Malaysians recently took matters into their own hands to clear a traffic bottleneck caused by a parked car on a narrow road. A video of the incident, which shows six people physically lifting and shifting the vehicle out of the way, has since gone viral online. Real 'Malaysia Boleh' energy," said a Threads user.

items.title: NIO inks battery-swapping deal with Geely, values energy unit at US$2.4bil
items.summary: Under the deal, Geely Holding Group will acquire a 30 per cent stake in NIO Power, NIO's battery-swapping and charging unit. The transaction values NIO Power at a post-money valuation of about 16 billion yuan (US$2.38 billion). NIO will acquire a 10 per cent equity stake in Geely's smart charging subsidiary, Haohan Energy.

items.title: Police confirm excavator operator drowned after machine overturned during Tasik Bera cleaning work
items.summary: KUANTAN, Sept 28 — An excavator operator was found drowned after the machine he was operating overturned during cleaning work at Tasik Bera, Bera yesterday. Bera district police chief Supt Zulkiflee Nazir said his team received a report regarding the incident at around 2.10pm Sunday. He said the deceased was Alief Daniel Haqim Abdullah, 26, while another worker who survived was Muhammad Aiman Fikri Mohd Azhar, 28.

items.title: 80-year-old man killed in Raub house fire
items.summary: RAUB: An 80-year-old man was killed after his house in Kampung Kuala Dong here was destroyed by fire last night. Pahang Fire and Rescue Department director Datuk Mohd Razam Taja Rahim said firefighters from the Raub station arrived at the scene at 10.20pm. After extinguishing the fire, firefighters inspecting the premises found the victim's remains in the living room.

items.title: Momenta, Stellantis' China JV with Dongfeng to co-develop intelligent driving technology
items.summary: BEIJING: Momenta, a Chinese maker of autonomous-driving software, has agreed to work with a Stellantis joint venture to develop advanced driver-assistance technology, it said on Monday, adding Jeep and Peugeot to its growing roster of global brands. In a statement, Momenta said it signed a global strategic partnership on Thursday to partner with Dongfeng Stellantis Automotive Technology (Wuhan) and the two Stellantis brands for intelligent driving technology. © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Ringgit opens higher against major currencies, lower vs US dollar
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit opened mostly higher against major currencies but slightly lower against the US dollar, with geopolitical uncertainties supporting demand for the greenback. At 8am, the ringgit eased to 4.0725/0780 versus the greenback from Friday's close of 4.0715/0765. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam told Bernama that geopolitical risk will continue to shape market sentiment as United States President Donald Trump has rejected Iran's plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

items.title: Tigray TV station hit by drone, rebels advance in north Ethiopia
items.summary: ADDIS ABABA: Ethiopia's army commander on Sunday accused Eritrea and Sudan of backing armed groups fighting its troops in the north of the country. Heavy clashes have resumed between the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF) and the federal government since Wednesday, raising fears of a return to a 2020-2022 civil war in which an estimated 600,000 people died. The TPLF has seized airports and launched attacks into the neighbouring states of Afar and Amhara, saying they were engaged in a "defensive war" against the government of Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed.

items.title: Johor air quality clears up, Serian lingers as Malaysia’s lone haze hotspot
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 28 — Serian in Sarawak was the only location in Malaysia recording an unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) reading as of 8.30am today, according to the Department of Environment (DoE). DoE surveillance data showed the monitoring station at IPD Serian logging an API reading of 152, placing it within the unhealthy threshold of 101 to 200. As of late yesterday afternoon, 51 monitoring stations nationwide, including the federal capital Kuala Lumpur, recorded moderate air quality, while 12 stations logged good air quality levels.

items.title: Science can guide wildlife-friendly road planning in Sabah
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: Scientific data on elephant movements along the Pan Borneo Highway has provided practical lessons on how road projects in Sabah can better account for wildlife. Universiti Malaysia Sabah senior lecturer Dr Nurzhafarina Othman said a project studying elephant movement and habitat use before and during highway construction in Tawai Forest Reserve had identified areas where wildlife activity overlapped with the highway alignment. Nurzhafarina said the issue went beyond individual road projects and reflected Sabah's broader development direction.

items.title: Foreigner feared drowned during raid
items.summary: KOTA BARU: An undocumented migrant is feared to have drowned after jumping into the Kelantan river while trying to flee a General Operations Force (GOF) raid here. GOF Southeast Brigade commander Senior Assistant Commissioner Ahmad Radzi Hussain said the operation, conducted with the Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA), was carried out along the riverbank in Kampung Lembah Sireh at 11.30pm yesterday. He said nine Indonesians, comprising six men and three women, and an Indian man were detained during the raid.

items.title: Gaza civil defense recovers remains of 28 Palestinians from house destroyed by Israel in 2023
items.summary: GAZA CITY: Gaza's Civil Defense said Sunday it had recovered the remains of 28 Palestinians from beneath the rubble of a house destroyed by the Israeli army in October 2023. The recoveries are part of the second phase of the Civil Defense's project to retrieve the remains of people buried beneath buildings destroyed during Israel's war on Gaza. The phase began on July 19 and covers sites in Gaza City, northern Gaza and the Nuseirat refugee camp.

items.title: Asean's voice took centre stage at a time world lost its balance
items.summary: NEW YORK: Asean is being increasingly recognised as an important voice in addressing a wide range of global issues, with its position often awaited by the international community. Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said the regional bloc has emerged as an influential middle power, driven by consensus among its member states in voicing issues related to peace, human rights and compliance with international law. "Asean's voice is now awaited by many countries and the international community because we speak as a united bloc.

items.title: Oil rebounds after Trump rejects Iran peace deal
items.summary: SINGAPORE: Oil prices rebounded more than one per cent on Monday after US President Donald Trump rejected a peace deal from Iran to resolve their conflict and reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Brent crude futures rose US$1.82, or 1.74 per cent, to US$106.14 a barrel by 2202 GMT while US West Texas Intermediate crude was at US$93.55 a barrel, up US$1.14, or 1.23 per cent. © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Iran wants Malaysia to continue encouraging peaceful dialogue with the US
items.summary: NEW YORK: Iran wants Malaysia to continue playing the role of a mediating voice on the international stage by encouraging diplomatic efforts between Teheran and Washington to continue in order to ease tensions that continue to grip the Middle East. Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said Malaysia remains committed to diplomatic channels, which are an important foundation for preventing any crisis from escalating or dragging on. He said Araghchi also briefed him on the latest developments in the crisis affecting the region, as well as Teheran's continued commitment to a diplomatic solution.

items.title: Serian air quality remains unhealthy
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Air quality in Serian, Sarawak remained unhealthy, with an Air Pollutant Index (API) reading of 151 as of 7am today. According to the Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS), 54 of 68 monitoring stations nationwide recorded moderate air quality, with readings between 51 and 100. The air quality is expected to gradually improve following forecasts of rain and thunderstorms in several areas nationwide from this afternoon.

items.title: Malaysia invited to co-chair The Hague Group
items.summary: NEW YORK: Malaysia has been invited to co-chair The Hague Group following the country's firm and consistent stance in advocating compliance with international law and addressing humanitarian issues on various global platforms. Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said several nations which were members of the group had voiced their desire for Malaysia to be co-chair with South Africa. Mohamad said Malaysia was a joint sponsor of The Hague Group at this year's UNGA.

items.title: Alberta, resources and the political economy of Canadian federalism
items.summary: But Alberta offers an unusually clear illustration of a more profound problem confronting modern federations: what happens when the geography of production no longer sits comfortably with the geography of political authority? It is about production federalism. Who regulates production?

items.title: Don't fear the Port Klang LCL fee hike just yet
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Businesses may not need to fear the proposed revision of Port Klang's less-than-container-load (LCL) charges just yet, as the impact is expected to vary between import and export shipments, according to industry players. While manufacturers and small and medium enterprises (SMEs) have raised concerns over higher logistics costs, freight-forwarding industry players said the proposed revision follows a roughly decade-long gap in the review of regulated LCL charges. According to Chia, the proposed revision covers charges imposed on LCL cargo at container freight stations (CFS) and warehouses, including facilities within port terminals.

items.title: Beyond the jab: The science and systems behind vaccination
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: FOR many people, a vaccine is simply a jab to prevent a disease. That makes continuous disease surveillance an essential part of vaccine policy. The data should cover invasive pneumococcal disease, circulating serotypes, vaccination status, breakthrough infections, antimicrobial resistance and vaccine coverage.

items.title: From mine to magnet: Malaysia's rare earths need more than a ban
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia needs to attract investors for rare earth elements (REE) who are willing to bring technology, capital and expertise into the country as it seeks to move beyond exporting raw materials and build higher-value industries around its critical mineral resources. Academy of Sciences Malaysia (ASM) Fellow and geologist P. Loganathan said restrictions on REE exports could encourage domestic processing and manufacturing, but would only deliver results if Malaysia developed capabilities across the entire value chain. According to Loganathan, Malaysia has not been exporting raw REEs or rare earth carbonates (RECs) under the current moratorium on raw mineral exports.

items.title: Serbia's President Aleksandar Vucic announces resignation
items.summary: BELGRADE: Serbia's long-time populist President Aleksandar Vucic resigned Sunday to run for prime minister in October snap elections after nearly two years of student-led protests that had been pressing for just such a poll. Vucic delivered his resignation speech from the presidential palace in Belgrade, where supporters gathered outside chanting his name. "I am resigning as president," Vucic said.

items.title: Boom gates, guardhouses and access cards: Here are 23 rules guarded Klang Valley neighbourhoods must follow
items.summary: In Kuala Lumpur, City Hall (DBKL) uses the PLANMalaysia guideline as a reference for guarded neighbourhoods. PLANMalaysia’s 2019 guideline was introduced to guide state and local authorities, technical agencies and residents’ associations in establishing and managing guarded communities in non-strata housing. It replaced the 2010 guideline.

items.title: Washington denounces Iran's truce proposal as 'cynical'
items.summary: WASHINGTON: A top US official on Sunday dismissed a proposal for reopening the Strait of Hormuz presented by Iran as "cynical" and indicated it was a non-starter for Washington. Iran's truce plan, announced by Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi at the United Nations earlier this week, calls for the release of frozen Iranian assets, the lifting of sanctions on Iranian oil and an end to the US naval blockade in order for the key waterway central to the world's energy supplies to be opened. US President Donald Trump rejected the deal on Saturday, stating that Iranian leaders wanted the deal because "they are losing so badly."

items.title: Eviction outrage fuels Madrid protest camp
items.summary: MADRID: A protest camp here grew to include dozens of tents yesterday after the eviction of an 87-year-old woman from her lifelong home triggered outrage over gaps in tenant protections. Government authorities put the turnout at around 25,000, while the Madrid Tenants' Union, which organised the protest, said over 300,000 had taken part. News agency EFE put the number at around 100 tents.

items.title: MCMC blocked 101.66m spoof calls over seven months
items.summary: KULAI: The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC), in collaboration with telecommunications service providers, blocked 101.66 million scam or spoof calls from February to August. Teo also said the MCMC would hold an online meeting with Meta today regarding complaints about blocked WhatsApp accounts. MCMC previously said it was investigating public complaints regarding WhatsApp accounts that were reported to have been hacked, blocked or no longer accessible.

items.title: Family spokesman: Malaysia sought wider Nepal search for 55 uncontactable citizens, but access was limited
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 27 — Malaysia initially requested that the search and rescue (SAR) operation involving 55 Malaysians who are still uncontactable in Nepal cover the area from Rasuwagadhi to Syabrubesi, but the national team was only allowed to conduct searches in certain areas. Malaysia Solidarity: Families in Hope (MASFIH) spokesman Dr Manivannan Rethinam said the matter was conveyed to the next of kin during a closed-door meeting with government agencies at Wisma Putra today. He said the families raised the question of why the Special Malaysia Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (SMART) operation was not focused on Rasuwagadhi, which is a border area between Nepal and Tibet, believed to be one of the last locations many Malaysians were involved.

items.title: Man dies of rabies in Kedah’s first human case in 28 years
items.summary: ALOR SETAR, Sept 27 — The State Health Department (JKN) of Kedah has reported the state’s first human rabies case since 1998, involving a 31-year-old man from Kubang Pasu who died today after being bitten by a stray dog in August. It said that the victim sought treatment at a healthcare facility after the incident but did not receive rabies post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP). “Following the confirmation, Kedah JKN, the Kubang Pasu District Health Office, the Kedah Veterinary Services Department and relevant agencies implemented control and prevention measures, including active case detection, health education, enhanced surveillance of animal-bite cases, risk assessment and control of stray animals in the affected area.

items.title: All Malaysian Indian Progressive Front seeks BN membership — and a shot at contesting Penang seats
items.summary: BUTTERWORTH, Sept 27 — The All Malaysian Indian Progressive Front (IPF) has applied to become a component party of Barisan Nasional (BN), with Penang as the starting point before the move is taken to the national level. “IPF hopes its application to become a BN component party will receive due consideration, with Penang serving as the starting point before the initiative is taken to the national level,” he said in his speech at the Penang IPF assembly here today. Musa said Penang IPF was among the organisations that had actively supported BN, including during by-elections and state elections.

items.title: Wisma Putra: Nepal weighs legal measures for those still unaccounted for after Aug 26 floods, including 55 Malaysians
items.summary: In a statement Sunday, Malaysia’s Foreign Ministry said the proposed measures are still subject to Nepal’s domestic legal processes and have yet to take effect. “The Malaysian government will also continue to engage with the Nepalese authorities and coordinate with Malaysian agencies on the relevant processes,” it said. The briefing involved the Malaysian Special Search and Rescue Team (SMART), Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM), Department of Chemistry Malaysia, Malaysian Embassy in Kathmandu, Malaysian Embassy in Beijing and National Registration Department (JPN).

items.title: RM1b resort, 700 jobs: Papar’s first five-star hotel due in 2027
items.summary: PAPAR, Sept 27 — Papar’s first five-star hotel, InterContinental Sabah Kota Kinabalu Resort in Melinsung, is expected to begin operations in December 2027. Papar Member of Parliament Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali said the RM1 billion project, developed by Taiwan-based Sinyi Group, covers more than 80 acres (32.4 hectares), with IHG Hotels & Resorts as its operating partner. “Sinyi Group finally chose Papar for its investment to develop an international-standard tourism destination, the InterContinental Sabah Kota Kinabalu Resort,” he said.

items.title: Dr Zaliha denies attending Myanmar refugee settlement ceremony, says viral claim is false
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 27 — Former minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Datuk Seri Dr Zaliha Mustafa denied allegations that she had attended, officiated, or been involved in any groundbreaking ceremonies for new settlements for Myanmar refugees. Dr Zaliha explained that based on the review, the circulated photo is believed to have been taken at the Asean Sustainable Urbanisation Forum (ASUF), Asean Governors and Mayors Forum (AGMF), and Meeting of Governors and Mayors of Asean Capitals (MGMAC) 2025 in the capital city on August 12, 2025. Meanwhile, Dr Zaliha said the allegation that she supported or facilitated the resettlement of new Myanmar refugees was also inconsistent with the record of actions she took while leading the Federal Territories Department.

items.title: RM1m haul as GOF intercepts 15,000 coffee seedlings at Tanah Merah roadblock
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Sept 27 — The General Operations Force (GOF) seized 15,000 robusta coffee seedlings and a lorry with a total value of RM1 million during a roadblock at Lalang Pepuyu, Tanah Merah, last night. GOF Southeast Brigade commander SAC Ahmad Radzi Hussain said a 27-year-old man who was driving the lorry was detained during the operation at 11.30pm. “The total value of the seizure was estimated at RM1 million, comprising the lorry worth RM250,000 and the coffee seedlings worth RM750,000,” he said in a statement today.

items.title: Anwar hails squash ace Ng Eain Yow after Asian Games gold secures LA28 Olympic berth
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 27 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim congratulated national squash ace Ng Eain Yow on defending his men’s singles gold medal at Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Games today. “Four years ago in Hangzhou, the gold went to Eain Yow. Well done, Eain Yow!”

items.title: Two men found dead in separate Alor Gajah incidents, police rule out foul play
items.summary: ALOR GAJAH, Sept 27 — Two men, aged 57 and 38, were found dead in separate incidents in Alor Gajah today. Alor Gajah district police chief Supt Ahmad Abu Bakar said police received a report regarding the discovery of a 57-year-old man at 11.30am in an abandoned shophouse in Cherana Putih, Taboh Naning. In a related development, Ahmad said the second case involved a 38-year-old man found dead in an apartment unit in Simpang Ampat at approximately noon.

items.title: JPJ seizes 3,790 luxury vehicles worth RM550m in nationwide crackdown since June 2025
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Sept 27 — A total of 3,790 luxury vehicles worth an estimated RM550 million were seized by the Road Transport Department (JPJ) under Ops Luxury from June 2025 to yesterday for various offences. JPJ senior director of enforcement Datuk Muhammad Kifli Ma Hassan said 785 vehicles were seized between June and December 2025, while another 3,005 were seized from January to September 26 this year. “Some luxury vehicle owners said they were reluctant to go to JPJ offices to renew their road tax because they had been blacklisted for previous offences.

items.title: A month without answers: Families of missing Malaysians told Nepal search may soon end
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 27 — After more than a month of waiting without news, the families of Malaysians still missing following the flood disaster in Nepal are beginning to resign themselves to all possibilities when informed that the government of that country is considering ending the search and rescue (SAR) operations. S. Sankara, the son of a missing Malaysian, said Wisma Putra informed them that the Nepalese government is expected to conclude the rescue operation phase soon before transitioning to recovery operations. “Based on the briefing received, the search and rescue operation is still ongoing at this time.

items.title: Dr Wan Azizah wants women to make up at least 30pc of PKR candidates in Melaka
items.summary: MELAKA, Sept 27 — The principle of justice must continue to be the cornerstone of PKR’s struggle as it faces the Melaka state election, said the party’s Advisory Council chairman Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail. That is what we uphold in our party and in our struggle,” she told reporters after launching the Melaka Wanita PKR election machinery here today. Also present were prime minister’s political secretary Datuk Azman Abidin and Melaka Wanita PKR chief Mahani Masban.

items.title: Families of 55 missing Malaysians in Nepal want moratorium to ease loans, insurance claims
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 27 — Families of 55 Malaysians still missing following the flash flood in Nepal have urged the government to consider a special moratorium on the victims’ financial commitments, as their families are now facing difficulties accessing the victims’ accounts and assets, insurance coverage, and managing their loans. Malaysia Solidarity: Families in Hope (MASFIH) spokesperson Dr Manivannan Rethinam said that after 33 days without certainty, financial and legal issues have become among the most pressing concerns for the families, particularly as some of the victims were the main breadwinners. Manivannan said the victims’ status as missing persons had placed various constraints on their families, as assets and financial commitments under their names could not be managed as usual.

items.title: Amanah sets sights on 18 seats for GE16, but concedes it could lose all but one
items.summary: SUBANG JAYA, Sept 27 — Parti Amanah Negara (Amanah) will identify its general election candidates early to allow them to introduce themselves to voters and to enable the party to make more systematic preparations. The party’s deputy president, Datuk Seri Dr Mujahid Yusof Rawa, said this move alongside strengthening the party’s machinery and narrative is crucial for Amanah to retain its existing seats and achieve its target of winning more seats in the 16th general election (GE16). He said Amanah aims to win at least 18 parliamentary seats in GE16, enabling the party to play a greater role in championing the interests of the ummah (Muslim community).

items.title: MCMC blocks 101.66 million scam calls with telcos under spoofing gateway from Feb to Aug 2026
items.summary: KULAI, Sept 27 — The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC), in collaboration with telecommunications service providers, blocked a total of 101.66 million scam or spoof calls from February to August. She said this when asked to comment on the number of scam calls blocked so far. Meanwhile, Teo said the MCMC will hold an online meeting with Meta tomorrow regarding public complaints concerning blocked WhatsApp accounts.

items.title: Calls unanswered, woman forces entry and finds fiancé dead in Melaka home
items.summary: ALOR GAJAH, Sept 27 — A woman was left heartbroken after finding her fiancé lying lifeless in his home, having failed to reach him since last night. The 38-year-old went to his house in Simpang Ampat around 11am today after growing anxious when her calls went unanswered, Harian Metro reported. Alor Gajah district police chief Superintendent Ahmad Abu Bakar said she had gone to the man’s residence to look for him after being unable to contact him.

items.title: MetMalaysia alerts seven states to evening thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds
items.summary: In Perak, the affected area is Hulu Perak, while in Kelantan, the warning covers Kuala Krai, Jeli, Tanah Merah, Machang and Pasir Puteh, MetMalaysia said in a statement. The warning also covers Besut, Setiu, Dungun, Kemaman, Marang and Hulu Terengganu in Terengganu; Pekan, Rompin and Jerantut in Pahang; and Kota Tinggi and Mersing in Johor. In Sabah, the warning covers the West Coast (Ranau, Tuaran, Kota Kinabalu, Kota Belud, Penampang and Papar), Interior (Keningau, Tambunan, Pensiangan, Sook, Tenom, Sipitang, Beaufort and Membakut), Kudat (Kota Marudu), and Sandakan (Kinabatangan and Sandakan).

items.title: Evening haze: Unhealthy air quality in five areas nationwide, Johor accounts for four and Sarawak one
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 27 — Five areas, four in Johor and one in Sarawak, recorded Air Pollutant Index (API) readings at an unhealthy level as of 4pm today. Meanwhile, in Sarawak, only Serian recorded an unhealthy API reading, at 141. A total of 51 areas, including Kuala Lumpur, recorded readings at a moderate level, while 12 areas recorded good readings.

items.title: Do not compare Penang’s mega projects with one year of Sabah road funding, state PKR tells PAS rival
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 27 — Transport infrastructure development in Sabah remains a priority for the Madani Government, with comparisons between states needing to take into account their respective scale and requirements, said Sabah PKR Information Chief Ahmad Farid Sainuri. He said Sabah’s roads still required serious attention, including faster completion of the Pan Borneo Highway to narrow the development gap between Sabah and Peninsular Malaysia. “We do not deny that Sabah’s roads still require serious attention.

items.title: BN chairman Zahid says coalition will end ties with Pakatan once Parliament dissolves
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 27 — Barisan Nasional chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi today made he saw no possibility of cooperation between his coalition and Pakatan Harapan (PH), amid talks that relations between the two sides have hit “an all time low”. Speaking at the 18th annual general assembly of the Malaysian Makkal Sakti Party at the World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur this afternoon, the Umno president “promised” that BN would “part ways” the moment Parliament is dissolved, in an apparent response to calls for the coalition to stop all forms of political cooperation with PH in the Unity Government. At the same event, Parti Makkal Sakti Malaysia president Datuk Seri RS Thanenthiran urged Zahid to pull BN out of the Unity government as soon as possible.

items.title: Fire Dept finds nine tiny rooms squeezed into office and turned into student dormitory in Terengganu
items.summary: KUALA TERENGGANU, Sept 27 — Small student dormitories built within an office premises were among the conditions detected today by the Terengganu Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) during the Ops Sepadu Premis Sarang Burung operation around Kuala Terengganu. The premises on the second floor had nine small rooms built separately and converted into student dormitories, in addition to being found non-compliant with several building safety regulations. The integrated operation was carried out at four locations, namely Jalan Masjid Abidin, Jalan Engku Pengiran Anom 2, Jalan Engku Sar and Jalan Sultan Zainal Abidin.
